title: Relational Design
description: Setting up PostgreSQL and a SQL client, then designing a relational schema: tables, primary and foreign keys, one-to-many and many-to-many relationships, turning a user story into tables, normalization basics, and writing CREATE TABLE with data types and constraints.
sourceCoverageNotes: Second-mate grouping decision, not syllabus: the calendar gives sql-jdbc-foundations no module grouping (matrix-v3 discrepancy source-gap-sql-jdbc-foundations-modules). This module is calendar day F19 (curriculum/snapshot/pep-curriculum.json /tracks/0/weeks/3/days/3), rows 0-4, one page per row (relation exact).

Planned module coding lab (lab plan in evidence/sql-jdbc-foundations/intake.md): schema design and CREATE TABLE practice tested with mvn -q -o test against a lab-created database on the learner-local PostgreSQL server through pgJDBC (no container); authored with its lab.json in the relational-design module PR, so moduleLabs stays empty until the lab exists.
